title: Catechism of the Catholic Church — Mercy and Sin
summary: Catholic teaching presents God's mercy as revealed in Christ and calls sinners to conversion, forgiveness and sacramental reconciliation. Mercy does not abolish moral truth; grace heals and restores the sinner.

title: St. John Paul II — Dives in Misericordia
summary: Dives in Misericordia teaches that Jesus Christ reveals and makes present the Father's mercy, especially through the Paschal Mystery, and that the Church is called to proclaim and practice mercy.

title: St. John Paul II — St. Faustina and Divine Mercy
summary: St. Faustina's mission is situated within the Church's proclamation of the mystery of Divine Mercy. Private devotional messages serve the Gospel and do not replace public Revelation.

title: National Shrine of The Divine Mercy — Chaplet
summary: The Chaplet of Divine Mercy is prayed on ordinary Rosary beads using the introductory prayers, the Eternal Father prayer on the large beads, For the sake of His sorrowful Passion on the small beads, and the Trisagion conclusion.

title: St. John Paul II — Rosarium Virginis Mariae
summary: The Rosary is a Christ-centered contemplative prayer in the company of Mary. The four sets of mysteries contemplate major events in Christ's life and saving work.

title: Second Vatican Council — Dei Verbum
summary: Dei Verbum teaches that Sacred Scripture is inspired and is to be read within the unity of Scripture, the living Tradition of the whole Church and the analogy of faith, with attention to literary forms and authorial intention.

title: Catechism — Sacred Scripture
summary: The Catechism presents the Church's canon of Scripture and Catholic principles for reading the Bible in the Spirit who inspired it and within the Church's living Tradition.

title: Catechism — The Sacrament of the Eucharist
summary: The Eucharist is the source and summit of Christian life. By the consecration, Christ becomes truly, really and substantially present; the Church uses the term transubstantiation for the change of the whole substance of bread and wine into Christ's Body and Blood.

title: Catechism — Sacrament of Penance and Reconciliation
summary: Christ entrusted the ministry of reconciliation to the Church. In the Sacrament of Penance, the penitent's contrition, confession and satisfaction meet Christ's forgiving action through the ministry of the priest.

title: Catechism — Sacrament of Baptism
summary: Baptism is the gateway to life in the Spirit and the foundation of Christian life. It frees from sin, gives new birth as a child of God and incorporates the baptized into Christ and the Church.

title: Catechism — Sacrament of Confirmation
summary: Confirmation completes baptismal grace with a special outpouring of the Holy Spirit, rooting the baptized more deeply in divine filiation and strengthening them to witness to Christ.

title: Catechism — Gifts and Fruits of the Holy Spirit
summary: The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit are wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety and fear of the Lord. The fruits of the Spirit are perfections formed in us as the first fruits of eternal glory.

title: CHARIS — Baptism in the Holy Spirit
summary: Within Catholic Charismatic Renewal, Baptism in the Holy Spirit is not a new sacrament. It is described as an experiential release or awakening of graces already given in sacramental Baptism and Confirmation, fostering conversion and mission.

title: CHARIS International — Catholic Charismatic Renewal
summary: CHARIS serves the diverse expressions of Catholic Charismatic Renewal, frequently described as a current of grace. Its service emphasizes baptism in the Holy Spirit, charisms, evangelization, Christian unity and service to the poor.

title: Pope Leo XIV — Address to Catholic Charismatic Renewal, 30 May 2026
summary: Pope Leo XIV addressed members of Catholic Charismatic Renewal in 2026, situating their prayer and charisms within ecclesial communion and the Church's mission.

title: Catechism — The Communion of Saints
summary: The communion of saints expresses the communion of holy persons and holy things in Christ. The Church recognizes the intercession and example of the saints while adoration belongs to God alone.

title: Catechism — Mary, Mother of Christ and Mother of the Church
summary: Catholic Marian doctrine is Christological: Mary is Mother of God because Jesus Christ is truly God and truly man. Her faith and discipleship are understood within the mystery of Christ and the Church.

title: Catechism — Christian Prayer
summary: Christian prayer is a covenant relationship with God in Christ. The Catechism treats blessing, adoration, petition, intercession, thanksgiving and praise, as well as vocal prayer, meditation and contemplative prayer.

title: Catechism — The Holy Trinity
summary: The central mystery of Christian faith is one God in three divine Persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The Persons are really distinct yet consubstantial, one divine nature.

title: Catechism — The Church
summary: The Church is the People of God, Body of Christ and Temple of the Holy Spirit. Catholic teaching understands episcopal ministry and the Petrine office within apostolic succession and ecclesial communion.

title: Catechism — Sacrament of Matrimony
summary: Matrimony is a covenant by which a baptized man and woman establish a partnership of the whole of life, ordered to the good of the spouses and the generation and education of children, raised by Christ to the dignity of a sacrament between the baptized. Individual canonical cases require competent Church authority.

title: Catechism — Anointing of the Sick
summary: The Anointing of the Sick gives the grace of the Holy Spirit to those seriously ill or weakened by age, uniting the sick person to Christ's Passion and strengthening them with peace and courage.

title: Catechism — Sacrament of Holy Orders
summary: Holy Orders is the sacrament through which the apostolic ministry continues in the Church in the orders of bishop, priest and deacon, each according to its proper degree and mission.

title: Catechism — Private Revelations and the Deposit of Faith
summary: Private revelations do not belong to the deposit of faith and do not improve or complete Christ's definitive Revelation. Their role can be to help people live the faith more fully in a certain period, under the discernment of the Church.

title: Catechism — Mission and Witness
summary: The Church is missionary by nature. Evangelization proclaims Christ and bears witness through holiness, charity, catechesis and respect for human freedom; conversion is ultimately the work of grace.
